# 2022 Arnaud Combier Chiroubles — Glorious Gamay
Wednesday, November 04, 2026
2022 Arnaud Combier Chiroubles
Now that November is here, it's time to find some wines to warm us up on those chilly evenings in front of the fireplace. Traveling south from Burgundy, we arrive in Beaujolais, a region that deserves a little more attention than it often gets. While many wine drinkers are familiar with Beaujolais-Villages and Beaujolais Nouveau, they may be missing out on some of the region's best offerings by overlooking its ten Cru appellations. Here, Gamay takes center stage, producing wines with character, freshness, and plenty of personality. If you haven't explored them yet, this week we are taking a look at one. Arnaud Combier built his reputation making characterful, minimally manipulated wines in Burgundy before turning his attention to Beaujolais. Drawing on his experience in the Mconnais and Chablis, Combier now works with growers and vineyards to produce wines that reflect their individual terroirs. His Chiroubles comes from steep, high-altitude slopes where pink granite soils and cooler growing conditions help preserve freshness and finesse. The vineyards, some with vines more than 50 years old, provide the foundation for a wine that highlights the aromatic, expressive side of Gamay. So let us introduce to you the 2022 Arnaud Combier Chiroubles ($32.99). This wine is one of Beaujolais' ten Cru appellations, known for producing elegant, fresh reds from the Gamay grape. Expect bright red-fruit flavors, mineral nuances, and refreshing acidity, balanced by juicy fruit and a crisp, refined structure. An appealing alternative to heavier reds, it pairs beautifully with roasted chicken, pork, charcuterie or a simple weeknight meal. After all, a good red wine doesn't need to be big and bold to make an impression. Please join us this Friday and Saturday as we pour the 2022 Arnaud Combier Chiroubles ($32.99) along with the 2025 Von Kisel Gruner Veltliner ($19.99) from Austria. # 2023 Holloran Pinot Noir — Halloran for Halloween
Wednesday, October 28, 2026
2023 Holloran Pinot Noir
Halloween is here, the harvest season is winding down and November is creeping up faster than a ghost in the night. As we dust off our favorite fall recipes and perhaps test-drive a few contenders for the Thanksgiving table, it's time to think about the wines that will make those dishes shine. So, let's venture out west to Oregon's Willamette Valley, where we find a Pinot Noir that's right at home with the flavors of fall. Eve and Bill Holloran began their winemaking journey in Oregon's Willamette Valley in 1999, when they purchased a historic vineyard on Worden Hill Road in Dundee and land in the Eola-Amity Hills. With harvest approaching that first year, they established their winery in a converted horse barn at their West Linn property, producing a little over 500 cases of wine in total. Over the years, the operation has grown to include several distinctive vineyard sites, including vines planted in the early 1970s. Today, Holloran remains committed to sustainable farming, organic and biodynamic practices and a hands-on approach that allows each vineyard's unique soils and character to shine through. Their 2023 Holloran Pinot Noir ($32.99) showcases the character of Oregon's Willamette Valley, blending carefully selected barrels from the winery's finest blocks in the Dundee Hills and Eola-Amity Hills. The fruit comes from some of Holloran's oldest vineyard sites, including Le Pavillon and ANA, with vines dating to the early 1970s, as well as La Chenaie. These vineyards benefit from volcanic-origin soils and meticulous, hands-on vineyard management. Made in Holloran's restrained, Old World-inspired style, the wine emphasizes purity of fruit, bright acidity and the distinctive character of its vineyard origins. While this wine is at home alongside a simple roast chicken, if you feel like venturing into some creative fall recipes such as a Cornish game hen stuffed with wild rice and mushrooms to roasted chicken or duck, this wine would make an ideal bottle to bring to the table. Please join us this Friday and Saturday as we pour the 2023 Holloran Pinot Noir ($32.99) along with the 2025 Arnaud Combier Blanc Sain Chardonnay ($28.99) a crisp, easy drinking French Chardonnay. # 2024 Barollet Montagny 1er Cru — Classic Côte Chalonnaise
Wednesday, October 21, 2026
2024 Colin Barollet Montagny 1er Cru Les Bouchots
With the holiday season fast approaching, we are constantly on the lookout for wines that will make your celebrations all the more special. Last week we headed to Bordeaux; this week our search takes us to Burgundy, where we've found a terrific white wine that deserves a place at your holiday table. Dating back to 1879, Domaine Colin Barollet is a Burgundy estate located in the celebrated region of Meursault right in the heart of the Côte de Beaune. Drawing on generations of winemaking expertise, the domaine focuses on expressing the character of Burgundy's varied vineyard sites, producing wines known for their elegance, finesse and balance. Its portfolio spans several Burgundy appellations, reflecting the region's distinctive terroirs and long tradition of winemaking. Today we present to you their 2024 Colin Barollet Montagny 1er Cru Les Bouchots ($39.99). Hailing from the Côte Chalonnaise in southern Burgundy, this Premier Cru Chardonnay offers an appealing introduction to the region's renowned white wines. The Montagny appellation is dedicated exclusively to Chardonnay, with its limestone-rich hillsides helping shape wines that balance freshness and minerality. Bright yellow with green hues, this wine offers an expressive nose of white flowers and a hint of lime. The palate is ample and beautifully balanced, with notes of citrus and honeysuckle leading to a long finish with a hint of mineral at the end. The Les Bouchots vineyard holds Premier Cru status, making this bottling an especially appealing choice for lovers of classic white Burgundy. Elegant and versatile, it pairs beautifully with roasted chicken, seafood and a number of autumn menus. # 2019 Chteau Lestage — A Little Bordeaux, A Lot of Value
Wednesday, October 14, 2026
2019 Chateau Lestage
As we pass the midpoint of October, the holidays are just around the corner and it's never too early to start looking for high-value wines that deliver the quality we want at a price we're comfortable paying. The Francos staff is always on the lookout for these finds, and this time our search takes us to a small but prestigious appellation in Bordeaux. Located in the heart of Bordeaux's Médoc peninsula, Chteau Lestage benefits from an excellent vineyard position near the highest point of the Médoc. Owned by the Chanfreau family since 1963, the estate's 46-hectare vineyard features a distinctive mix of Pyrenean gravel, clay-limestone, and marl soils. Merlot plays a leading role in the blend, complemented by Cabernet Sauvignon and Petit Verdot, producing reds that balance ripe fruit and generous texture with the structure and elegance expected of a classic Médoc. With a long history in the Cru Bourgeois classification, Chteau Lestage is a fine example of Listrac-Médoc's ability to deliver traditional Bordeaux character and quality. This brings us to our featured wine, the 2019 Chteau Lestage ($34.99). The Cru Bourgeois classification is one of Bordeaux's best-kept secrets for value, offering classic regional character at prices that can be remarkably approachable. Within its three quality tiers, Chteau Lestage has achieved the highest level, Exceptionnel. Merlot-dominant, with a generous proportion of Cabernet Sauvignon, the wine is made from sustainably cultivated vineyards and aged for 12 months primarily in used oak barrels, allowing the fruit and terroir to take center stage. The 2019 vintage reveals aromas of ripe blackcurrant and blackberry, layered with hints of spice and toasted oak. On the palate, generous dark fruit meets fresh acidity and fine, structured tannins, creating a balanced, age-worthy expression of old-world Bordeaux. For fall menus, pair it with herb-crusted roast lamb, grilled New York strip, braised short ribs, or a slow-cooked beef stew. If you're looking for classic, age-worthy Bordeaux at a remarkable price, Chteau Lestage deserves a place at the table. EAT SLEEP WINE REPEAT: A Wine Podcast Exploring Wine Regions, Grapes & Education
Hey there! If you love wine, are curious about the world’s wine regions, or just want to geek out a little on grapes, terroir, and winemaking, you’re in the right place. This is a fun, educational wine podcast made for serious enthusiasts, wine students, and anyone who wants to fall in love with wine all over again. I chat with winemakers, sommeliers, and Masters of Wine who share their stories, tips, and insider knowledge - from their favourite regions and grapes to food pairings and the techniques that make each bottle special. Sometimes we open a bottle as we talk, sometimes I take you along on a 4-day itinerary I’ve mapped out from my travels, and sometimes we do quick-fire flashcard-style deep dives to test your wine knowledge - all in a way that’s engaging, uplifting, and never boring. Whether you’re working towards your WSET or MW exams, or just want to explore the world of wine with a glass in hand, this podcast is a place to laugh, learn, and celebrate the joy of wine. Come join our inclusive wine-loving community - there’s a story, a tip, or a tasting for everyone.
Informative Host, Great Guests, and Fun Topics!
Mar 16
My go to wine podcast. Always puts me in a good mood just listening to it and taking in the wide world of wine!
The best wine podcast, and a fantastic one independent of the topic!
07/09/2024
Ok, what do you want from a wine podcast? TLDR: whatever it may be, you will find it in Eat Sleep Wine Repeat. Most wine podcasts are informative. In fact, the main driver of the topic of wine is to educate. The world of wine is so wide and deep that one could talk endlessly about it. But that’s the problem — some wine podcasts become a dragging drone of facts. Not Janina. For sure, she will educate you. You will learn all the facets of wine. Not just the characteristics of specific wines, but history, geography, geology, economics, and even culture. Covering all this could result in dry lecture, but Janina is such a talented presenter that she effortlessly weaves all these facts into the larger story she is telling about wine. Some wine podcasts are entertaining. But rarely. Most that try to be entertaining end up being gimmicky. Often these cannot be sustained for long as the act becomes repetitive. Not Janina. Janina is a natural communicator. Her fluid presentation masks the fact that she probably puts in a serious effort to tell a solid story. If you watch any of her YouTube videos, you might notice that they are all a single take — no editing. But she speaks with such richness, depth, and passion that you may not even notice that she pulled off a complex effort in presentation. You notice this in her podcasts too. There are frequent guests, but these always feel like conversations, not interviews. I always feel like I am listening to a passionate discussion between two experts with a common love of the subject. You see it on Instagram. She’s not trying to be a viral influencer. Sure, her short videos are entertaining and engaging. But then look at the depth of information she puts in the notes. If you string them together you would get the knowledge base of a textbook, the entertainment of a graphic novel, and be engagement of a short story. But you get the full depth of Janina with her podcast. On the surface, you might wonder how much can anyone talk about a single topic and not get repetitive or run out of substance. Well, Janina goes into depth on the topic but keeps it lively. Her passion for all things wine and natural charisma comes through. Here’s another subtle demonstration of how seriously Janina takes her mission. All her podcast descriptions have an annotated timeline of the entire episode. This makes it so easy to use the podcast as a reference — to return at a later time to a specific point. If you want to be educated about wine, this is the podcast for you. If you simply love wine, you will love this podcast. Heck, if you just barely know wine but want to learn from someone who won’t talk above you or talk down to you (it takes skill to walk that fine line), you will like this podcast. I just cannot get enough of the good stuff — this podcast!
